recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If generated profile snapshots become stale again, investigate the publisher/snapshot-generation pipeline or generated publication artifacts rather than changing current differential/spreadsheet source inputs unless a specific source profile is shown to be wrong.
issue_request: FHIR-13172 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction raised for DSTU2 and applied for R5. It asked to regenerate STU3 publication snapshots after snapshot generation code had been corrected so slicing would work in generated snapshots.
initial_application: No git commit mentioning FHIR-13172 was found. The closest historical implementation evidence is commit 624febd12341a765f1037995e61b839b3c2dd81c, which fixed snapshot-generation tooling around propagating differential extensions into snapshots and added a snapshot-generation test case, but it did not tag the Jira. The Jira has no comments, and FHIR-I minutes from 2020-01-20 record only that FHIR-13172 would be fixed as a tooling issue.
additional_context: Current build-scope profile inputs are active through source/fhir.ini's [profiles] entries, while legacy us-core and cda profile inputs are commented out there. Current core profile source candidates under source/profiles and resource profile StructureDefinitions do not contain checked-in <snapshot> sections; they contain spreadsheets and differentials that the publisher regenerates into snapshots. Searches found no Zulip discussion for FHIR-13172 and no Confluence evidence beyond the FHIR-I minutes.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The requested action was regeneration of historical generated snapshots with corrected tooling, and the current authoritative source does not carry stale checked-in snapshots that could be repaired by a source change.
